question: Given a pool that contains a reviewed implementation of a required capability, does the solver reuse it, and does it fail closed with an explicit reason when the pool does not qualify?
why_this_exists: The retired Duplicate Finder workload measured code generation. Its component decisions recorded only the Python standard library, so it never observed reuse.
The calibration and system-E2E workloads execute a composition a human already chose, so they measure execution, not selection.
Selection is the product claim. Until this benchmark, nothing measured it.

cases.expected: complete plan, grounded-researcher-v1 selected, zero adapters, zero generated files
cases.measures: reuse of a qualified reviewed component

cases.expected: complete plan on the qualified alternative; the higher-priority blocked entry is never selected
incomplete plan; reason 'evidence L3 is below required L4'
cases.measures: the evidence ladder is not lowered to complete a plan

cases.expected: incomplete plan; reason 'license GPL-3.0-only is not allowed'
cases.measures: license policy is enforced before selection

cases.expected: incomplete plan; both the launch lock and the review promotion binding reject the drift
cases.measures: supply-chain identity is verified independently at two boundaries

cases.expected: incomplete plan with an eligible component and the 'no complete contract route' warning
cases.measures: an unroutable graph is reported distinctly from an empty pool

measurement_rules: The evaluator owns the expected outcomes. A candidate may not read or modify it during measurement.
A case file whose SHA-256 differs from this manifest invalidates the run.
Re-freezing the cases after a component or review changes is a deliberate, separately reviewed act.
A complete plan is selection evidence only. It is not an L4 system-verification verdict.
The executable case must produce a schema-valid required output through the real component process.
limitations: The pool holds one capability and one reviewed implementation, so this benchmark does not measure multi-capability routing or adapter synthesis.
It measures the deterministic solver. It says nothing about discovery quality or about whether a better component exists upstream.
Passing every case is not evidence that an arbitrary real-world system can be composed.
